Revision 2.4 — final candidate: rail cleanup, rotation, canonical palette, sparkles, target containment Direct owner review of the 2.3.2 exports found five real bugs surviving in the evidence, all fixed here without reopening the locked topology, charge model, primary-selection algorithm, or source assets. (1) Closed-state rails: the "detached teal line" in spawn Frames 1/2 and extraction Frames 6/7 was never a leftover authoring guide — .kf-target had no definite height of its own (it depended on in-flow children to stretch it), so any frame with an empty or fully position:absolute target collapsed to 0 content height, leaving only its own 1px+1px border visible as a flat bar. Fixed with one rule: aspect-ratio:1 on .kf-target, tying its height to its own real width regardless of children. This also fixed the start-anchor rings, which had been rendering as squashed ellipses in that same collapsed box. (2) Diamond rotation: edge-diamond-energized.png's alpha channel was measured directly — its brighter tip sits at (920,131) against a (627,627) canvas center, a native resting angle of -59.43deg. Every shell that has a real target direction (all four perimeter primaries, the beam-target study, spawn, extraction, scale-proof) now rotates so that measured tip visibly leads to its target, via one shared rotForVector() helper — not left in one fixed orientation. (3) Beam-port seam: a new close-up study (Diamond & beam-port proof, Section D) shows the measured port before rotation and the same shell rotated and zoomed tight against the conduit, proving the beam originates from the shell's visible tip and not empty canvas space. (4) Canonical energy material: the conduit/packet gradient was a bespoke cool-only 4-stop bar; both now consume --energy-material, the same palette-stops contract Navigation Core Revision 6.1 locked for the trail (cyan/blue/violet/magenta dominant, brief red/orange/yellow/green accents), animated as one continuous traveling phase — the packet's ring uses the identical gradient/animation as the conduit rather than an unrelated lavender. (5) Sparkles and containment: every decorative shell glint (charge states, absorb, waking/peak) is now the same four-point twinkle mark used elsewhere in Mazer, staggered per instance, replacing plain circular dots; and the start-tile's contained energy now visibly peaks (a full --energy-material flare fills the tile) the instant the packet arrives, instead of holding one flat intensity throughout.

Real finding — the codebase already solved this, by texture-swap not compositing edge-diamond-energized.png and edge-diamond-iridescent.png share one silhouette family: a long, diagonal, four-pointed shard. edge-diamond-energy-core.png is visually a completely different object — a symmetric, vertically-oriented nested-diamond outline with a thin ring crossing it. Stacking its full 1254×1254 canvas onto the shard shell puts two unrelated diamond silhouettes on screen at once, which is exactly the defect a real code comment in BootScene.ts describes. The actual fix already shipped: edge-diamond-energized.png is its own second-pass render with the energy linework baked into the same image, used as a straight texture swap in place of iridescent.png — zero runtime compositing. energy-core.png stays reference-only, useful only as the negative example below (Section B, Treatment 1).
CUR

Current system — what actually ships today Current, verified

Real, shipped, in src/legacy-runtime/legacyPlayerTransfer.ts and its call sites in MenuScene.ts — not a menu-only flourish. This is the visual language the proposed sections below extend, not replace.

idle → pending (armed on goal reach, waiting for deconstruction to start) → outbound (450ms, energy travels from the old goal outward — first ~52% invisible, then fades in) → stored (holding, gentle sine-wave alpha breathing) → delivering (aligned to the bleed-off corridor reaching the screen edge on the next maze) → complete

Verified facts

  • Not one effect — a multi-origin, multi-phase handoff. outbound (goal reach arms it, energy runs during deconstruction, all 8 origins converge on the old goal) → stored (holding, breathing alpha) → delivering (aligned to the bleed-off corridor reaching the screen edge on the next build). Any directional claim below is tied to one of these named phases, not the system as a whole.
  • Trigger: real play goal-reach (nextStep.reachedGoal) and the menu demo's own goal-reach both call armLegacyPlayerTransferEnergy.
  • Diamond shell: edge-diamond-energized.png only — used continuously, no idle/charged texture distinction exists today.
  • Diamond count (outbound phase): all 8 orbit-sigil positions participate every time — "every diamond fires, not just the ones that happen to sit on a true corner" (code comment).
  • Beam: genuinely wired — playerTransferBeamStripImages / playerTransferBeamTargetCapImages, cropped from teleport-beam-iridescent.png at render time, with a double-ring impact flash on arrival.
  • Surfaces: menu demo and real play share the exact same code path (drawDynamicBoard) — "no mode branch."
  • Coordinate spaces differ: the diamonds (titleOrbitDiamondImages) live in boardZoomContainer (board-space, scales with board zoom); the beam and burst graphics (playerTransferBeamStripImages, playerSpawnBurstGraphics) are added directly to the scene (screen-space, top-level) — verified from the actual `add()`/`add.container()` call sites, not assumed.
  • Unused today: edge-diamond-iridescent.png, edge-diamond-energy-core.png, edge-diamond-energy-absorption-state.png — loaded in BootScene.ts, never imported in MenuScene.ts.
  • No deterministic source/destination diamond exists — the bleed-off corridor affects when delivery fires, not which diamond is treated as primary.
  • Renderer constraint: Mazer runs Phaser in Canvas mode (type: Phaser.CANVAS), where Image.setTint()/setTintFill() don't behave as they would under WebGL — a real code comment in BootScene.ts documents this and explains why tile-font color variants had to be pre-baked rather than tinted. Any proposed "charge" treatment below has to work within that constraint.

Diamond containment study

Revised from Revision 1: Treatment 2 now matches the real codebase precedent (one baked shell, not live compositing) instead of proposing a new derivative. Three options at one representative screen-edge scale; the failure mode is reproduced deliberately in Treatment 1 so the win in Treatment 2 is a visible contrast, not just a claim.

Rejected

1 · Naive full-canvas stack

edge-diamond-energy-core.png composited at full size, same position as the shell. Two different silhouettes overlap — this is the recorded defect, reproduced on purpose.

Real precedent — recommended

The shipped fix: edge-diamond-energized.png already has the energy linework baked into its own render. No compositing, no derivative. Note: this is the shell for containment purposes only — Section C locks a further decision that this same shell (not a swap to iridescent.png) is also used for every ambient/idle state, distinguished by opacity alone.

Not needed

Kept only to show it was considered. Treatment 2 already IS the real energy detail baked into real art at zero extra cost — this CSS pulse would be a downgrade, not an alternative.

C

Maze-build charge sequence Proposed target

Not current behavior — the real runtime uses energized.png continuously with no idle/charged distinction at all (see Current system, above). Decision from the registration study below: the idle(iridescent)→charged(energized) crossfade is retired. One shell, energized.png, used at every state — silhouette, center, and footprint never change. Charge reads through opacity, a contained procedural glow, internal glints, and pulse instead, which also respects the Canvas-renderer tint constraint noted in Current system.

Measured registration check — why the crossfade was retired edge-diamond-iridescent.png's own content bounding box is not identical to edge-diamond-energized.png's: iridescent is ~4% wider, ~7% taller, and its center sits 21px right, 9px down from energized's center on the shared 1254×1254 canvas (≈1.7% / 0.7% of canvas width/height). The overlay below shows both at 60% opacity, stacked — real measurement, not a redraw, and the doubled edges are visible. That's enough to retire the crossfade rather than risk a runtime-visible jump.

E

Player spawn-in sequence Proposed target

More elaborate than the current system's real delivery step (single beam volley + impact flash, see Current system above). This proposes a deliberate materialization choreography using the Navigation Core v1 player/start-marker language:

1 perimeter diamond wakes  →  2 inner energy contracts  →  3 beam opens toward start tile  →  4 start-anchor brightens  →  5 player begins materializing  →  6 player reaches full one-cell form  →  7 beam collapses  →  8 post-spawn residue remains  →  9 diamond returns to ambient

Static contact sheet — 7 approval checkpoints

F

Player extraction sequence Proposed target

The current system's outbound phase already moves energy away from the goal on completion — this proposes making that moment more deliberate, and gives it somewhere to go: not spawn reversed frame-for-frame, using edge-diamond-energy-absorption-state.png's own dark-shard-in-swirl language (currently unused, reference-only) for the absorb moment:

1 goal accepted  →  2 destination diamond wakes  →  3 energy surrounds player  →  4 player contracts into energy  →  5 beam connects player tile to diamond  →  6 energy travels toward diamond  →  7 diamond absorbs it  →  8 beam collapses  →  9 diamond settles, transition commits

G

Perimeter topology — current vs. proposed

This is exactly where current and proposed diverge most. Not approved — a comparison to judge, not a fait accompli.

Rendered proof — 390×844 representative viewport, all four primary-edge cases

One primary anchor at 100% (~15–22% for the other seven during an active transfer, shown here), HUD/safe-area exclusion zones, a target tile, and a thin conduit — for each of the four edges a primary anchor could sit on.

Current, verified

  • All 8 orbit-sigil diamonds exist and all 8 fire on every transfer.
  • The outbound phase uses a slightly staggered eight-origin converging volley, landing as one double-ring impact flash; stored and delivering follow under the existing transfer lifecycle (see Current system, above).
  • Identical behavior on the menu demo and real play — one shared code path.
  • No diamond is ever more "primary" than another — the effect is symmetric by design.
  • No HUD-avoidance logic needed today because the effect is brief and self-contained.

Proposed — awaiting approval

  • All 8 ambient diamonds stay visible (identity preserved) but drop to ~25–35% intensity when not in use.
  • One diamond becomes the deterministic primary anchor for a given spawn/extraction (selection rule locked below).
  • One primary beam carries the actual transfer; other diamonds may show restrained synchronized glints, not full beams.
  • The current full 8-way volley is preserved as a menu/title-only flourish, or an exceptional/celebratory effect — not the default gameplay transfer.
  • Needs real HUD/safe-area exclusion zones once a primary diamond can sit anywhere near application chrome.
  • Persists across the whole handoff: the same primary anchor stays selected through outbound → stored → delivering — it isn't re-picked per phase.
Proposed deterministic selection rule (locks Q7) 1. Candidate set: all 8 fixed perimeter anchors. 2. Exclude/penalize any anchor overlapping HUD or safe-area exclusion zones. 3. Of the remaining valid anchors, choose the one whose inward beam origin is closest to the extraction target. 4. Break ties by a fixed anchor-ID order — never randomly. 5. Persist that anchor through stored and delivering. 6. Only remap, deterministically to the nearest still-valid anchor in the same perimeter sector, if a viewport or safe-area change invalidates the held anchor mid-transfer.

I

Reduced motion

Same states as spawn/extraction, no travel. No orbiting title-sigil spin, no traveling shine, no repeated pulse — short crossfades between hard states instead. The live artifact still animates; this describes the reduced-motion behavior the runtime should implement (matches the prefers-reduced-motion handling already established for Navigation Core's trail and end star).

Spawn: charged diamond (static) → beam appears at full length instantly (short fade-in) → start anchor changes state (no pulse) → player fades in over one short crossfade → beam fades out. No orbit, no travel, no particles.

Extraction: player present (static) → beam appears instantly → player crossfades out → diamond swaps to its absorbed/settled look → beam fades out. Same hierarchy, no motion in between.

Q

Owner decisions

1
Which shell is canonical for active teleport use? Resolved — energized.png alone, in every state including ambient/idle (opacity ~28% at rest). iridescent.png is not used as a swap target anywhere in the proposal (Section C's registration study is why).
2
Which containment treatment wins? Resolved — Treatment 2, the real precedent (one baked shell, zero compositing). Treatments 1 and 3 are kept only as the rejected/unnecessary comparison.
3
Full replacement, masked overlay, or reference-only? Resolved — reference-only for v1. The extraction absorb/stored states use the same locked energized.png shell (contained internal flare + glints), never a silhouette swap.
4
Beam composition — cap+tiled-center+cap (Section D) or a fully procedural centerline with only the two caps as real source art?
5
How much glow overflow is permitted around the active diamond, relative to its own icon bounds?
6
Does energy visibly travel along the beam (a moving highlight), or does the beam stay a stable conduit while only the source/target states change?
7
Which diamond is selected? Resolved — see Section G's deterministic selection rule (closest valid anchor, HUD/safe-area excluded, persists through the whole handoff).
8
Do inactive perimeter diamonds stay visible (dimmed) during an active sequence, or fade out to reduce noise?
9
Preferred total perceived duration for one spawn or extraction transition — quick (under 1s), moderate (1-2s), or deliberate (2s+)?
10
Reduced motion — which states remain as hard cuts (idle / charged / beam / player-present / player-gone), and which motion is cut entirely?
